fields.study_design: narrative review and policy perspective (comment article; selective synthesis, not a systematic review)
fields.population: population of the Democratic Republic of Congo, with focus on rural and conflict-affected provinces (North Kivu, Kasai, Tanganyika, South Kivu)
fields.sample_size: not stated: PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar and Web of Science searched for peer-reviewed literature up to August 2025 plus WHO, UNICEF and DRC Ministry of Public Health documents; no counts of records screened or included; the authors state the method is a selective synthesis, not a systematic review
fields.effect_measure: narrative thematic synthesis (WASH relevance to NTD transmission, obstacles in DRC, integration opportunities); no pooled estimate
fields.effect_estimate: Reported (not appraised): safe water, sanitation and hygiene interrupt transmission of schistosomiasis, soil-transmitted helminths, trachoma, Guinea worm and, indirectly, lymphatic filariasis; improved sanitation is quoted as reducing schistosomiasis by 77% and trachoma by 27% (global figures from other sources). DRC barriers: armed conflict in the eastern provinces destroying WASH infrastructure, poor health and water governance, and under-funded infrastructure; Kinshasa has about 70% improved water coverage while rural areas such as North Kivu are below 30%. No evidence links specific integrated WASH-NTD programmes to reductions in NTDs in DRC. Recommendations: community-managed borehole committees, mobile WASH units in conflict areas, school WASH and NTD education, multi-level governance with accountability, country-specific monitoring.
fields.section: Full text (9 pages): Methodology; Burden of NTDs; Linking WASH and NTDs (Table 1); Challenges; Strategies; Recommendations; Limitations
fields.exact_location: Methodology (p. 2); Challenges section (p. 5: conflict, governance, 70% vs 30% coverage); Strategies and Recommendations (pp. 6-7); Limitations (p. 8)

evidence_level: Single-source evidence: a narrative review and policy perspective (comment article) on WASH and neglected tropical diseases in the DRC; no systematic method, no counts, no primary data; read in full text 2026-10-04.
pdf_note: Discover Social Science and Health 5:147, English, 9 pages read in full (Drive file S322_Ojo_Akosile_2025...pdf)
notes: ELIGIBILITY FLAG: a comment/narrative review with no primary data and no systematic method; inclusion criterion 3 (empirical evidence or systematic empirical synthesis) is doubtful, and the exposure is health integration (WASH in NTD programmes) rather than a legal or administrative factor. Candidate for the criterion-3 audit (A22).
